outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Chips & AI infrastructure, led by Nvidia, AMD, TSM, and Cadence
strongest.reason: the group rebounded together heading into Nvidia's closely watched after-the-bell Q2 report, recovering much of yesterday's pre-earnings pullback

strongest.area: Beaten-down enterprise software, led by Salesforce, ServiceNow, and the broader SaaS complex (monday.com, HubSpot, Intuit)
strongest.reason: continues to hold recent gains as capital keeps rotating out of richly valued, capex-heavy AI names and into subscription-model software that doesn't carry the AI infrastructure bill

weakest.reason: pulled back after briefly topping $81,000 overnight, as the Clarity Act's Senate cloture vote now has a firm but more distant date of September 15

weakest.area: AI software and cloud laggards, led by Adobe, Palantir, and Oracle
weakest.reason: each gave back ground today — Adobe and Palantir cooling after recent run-ups, and Oracle continuing to lag megacap-cloud peers on capex and free-cash-flow concerns

outlook.nextStep: Nvidia's Q2 report lands after today's close and is the single biggest near-term catalyst, given how directly today's chip-sector rebound seems tied to it; Fed Chair Warsh's Friday Jackson Hole speech is the other major event worth close attention for rates and macro. The software rotation and crypto's now-dated September 15 Clarity Act vote are probably better treated as slower-moving stories to watch than as near-term events to react to.

signals.title: Chips rebound together into Nvidia's after-the-bell Q2 report
signals.body: Nvidia, AMD, TSM, and Cadence all traded higher today, recovering much of yesterday's pre-earnings pullback, ahead of Nvidia's Q2 report due after the close. Analysts are modeling roughly $93-95B in revenue (about 95% year-over-year growth), with price targets clustering between $275 and $325. Nvidia's own stock snapped a seven-day losing streak, its longest since 2022, on the move.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether tonight's results confirm the AI-infrastructure demand story or reignite the ROI-fear narrative from earlier this summer

signals.title: Bond-market anxiety persists ahead of Warsh's Friday Jackson Hole debut
signals.body: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole keynote Friday, August 28, around 10 a.m. ET. Fed watchers describe him as a closed book on forward guidance; after the July meeting he offered little insight into his views, and long-term yields subsequently climbed to a two-decade high. The 10-year yield eased slightly today but remains elevated heading into the speech.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at how directly Warsh addresses the rate path Friday, given how sensitive yields have been to his prior public comments

signals.title: Bitcoin cools after topping $81,000 as the Clarity Act vote gets a firm September 15 date
signals.body: Bitcoin briefly broke above $81,000 overnight before pulling back roughly 2% on the day. The Senate has now scheduled a cloture vote on the Clarity Act for September 15, requiring 60 votes to pass; with 53 Republicans, seven Democrats would need to join. Coinbase's CEO has said he expects passage, though prediction markets are less confident.
signals.focus: worth watching whether sentiment holds through the three-week wait to the actual vote, versus treating the current pullback as the rally cooling off

signals.title: Software rotation broadens beyond the original names, but today saw some cooling
signals.body: The rotation out of AI hardware into beaten-down enterprise software has spread further, with monday.com, HubSpot, and Intuit joining Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Adobe in recent gains. Today, however, ServiceNow, Salesforce, Adobe, and Palantir all eased back slightly, suggesting the move may be pausing after a strong one-to-two week run.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether this is a brief pause in the rotation or a sign it's starting to unwind

signals.title: Zscaler extends its rally while CrowdStrike cools slightly ahead of earnings
signals.body: Zscaler built on last week's KeyBanc and Mizuho price-target hikes with another sharp gain today, while CrowdStrike eased back modestly heading into its Q2 report, even after KeyBanc's recent price-target increase to $240.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether CrowdStrike's upcoming report can reignite the same momentum currently favoring Zscaler

signals.title: China's humanoid-robotics complex rebounds after recent weakness
signals.body: UBTECH and the broader China humanoid-robotics and industrial-automation space bounced back today after a recent pullback, part of a sector-wide recovery. Tesla also continued to lean further into its own Optimus narrative as a growing share of its long-term enterprise value.
signals.focus: worth treating single-day swings in individual robotics names as noise relative to the multi-year capital-flow trend into the space
